title: How does an airplane stay in the air?
sources: FAA Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge

lines.text: How does a massive commercial airliner weighing over five hundred tons stay airborne without falling?
lines.caps: How does a *500-ton plane | stay in the | *air?

lines.text: It all comes down to the curved aerodynamic shape of the wings, called an airfoil.
lines.caps: The secret is the *curved | wing called an | *airfoil

lines.text: Jet engines blast the aircraft forward, forcing air to rush over and under the wings.
lines.caps: Engines thrust the *plane | forward at high | *speed

lines.text: Air flowing over the curved top travels faster, creating an area of low pressure above the wing.
lines.caps: Air moves *faster on top | creating low | *pressure

lines.text: Meanwhile, higher pressure beneath the wing physically pushes the entire aircraft upward.
This aerodynamic upward force is called lift, and once it exceeds the airplane's weight, it flies.
lines.caps: This upward force is *lift | overcoming total | *weight!

lines.text: At five hundred miles per hour, air turns into a solid, invisible cushion.
lines.caps: Air turns into an *invisible | cushion of solid *support!
